Original Title & English Translation: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium libri VI (Six Books on the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Nuremberg: Johannes Petreius, 1543 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated heliocentric planetary kinematics; replaced Ptolemaic equant with double epicyclets and the Tusi couple to preserve uniform circular components; established orbital radii proportional to period.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the equant non-uniformity bottleneck of Ptolemy's Almagest; enabled Reinhold (B1-004) to compute Copernican tables and Kepler (B1-028) to seek physical solar causes.

Scientist: Archimedes of Syracuse (c. 287–c. 212 BCE), ed. Thomas Venatorius (1488–1551)
Original Title & English Translation: Archimedis Syracusani philosophi ac geometrae excellentissimi Opera, quae quidem extant, omnia (Extant Works of Archimedes: Equilibrium of Planes, Floating Bodies, Quadrature of the Parabola)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Basel: Johannes Hervagius, 1544 (editio princeps Greek & Latin)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Restored rigorous Euclidean deduction to statics (law of the lever, center of gravity of plane figures) and hydrostatics (buoyancy principle: upward force = weight of displaced fluid).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the qualitative Aristotelian dynamics bottleneck of Scholastic physics; directly provided the mathematical foundation for Tartaglia (B1-003), Benedetti (B1-005), Commandino (B1-007), and Stevin (B1-016).

Original Title & English Translation: Quesiti et inventioni diverse (Various Questions and Inventions), Books I & II
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Venice: Venturino Ruffinelli, 1546
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proved empirically that projectile trajectories are continuously curved throughout (rejecting the tripartite straight-arc-straight path); demonstrated that an elevation angle of 45° yields maximum ballistic range.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the scholastic bottleneck of violent vs. natural disjoint motions; directly stimulated Benedetti (B1-005) on continuous impetus and Galileo (B1-050) on parabolic ballistics.

Original Title & English Translation: Prutenicae Tabulae Coelestium Motuum (Prussian Tables of Celestial Motions)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Tübingen: Ulrich Morhart, 1551
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First comprehensive astronomical ephemeris calculated entirely from Copernican heliocentric parameters; standardized tabular computation of uniform circular planetary anomalies without Ptolemy's equant.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the observational inaccuracy and computational divergence of the Alfonsine Tables; provided Tycho Brahe (B1-010) the reference benchmarks that revealed persistent orbital errors.

Original Title & English Translation: Resolutio omnium Euclidis problematum aliorumque una tantummodo circini data apertura (Letter on Falling Bodies in Preface)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Venice: Bartolomeo Cesano, 1553
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the first mathematical proof that bodies of the same material but unequal weight fall through a given medium at identical speeds; speed of fall determined by specific gravity difference (v proportional to rho_body - rho_med).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Aristotelian speed-proportional-to-weight fallacy; directly sparked Benedetti's dedicated 1554 treatise (B1-006) and Galileo's early Pisan dynamics (B1-020).

Original Title & English Translation: Demonstratio proportionum motuum localium contra Aristotelem et omnes philosophos (Demonstration of Proportions of Local Motions against Aristotle)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Venice: Bartolomeo Cesano, 1554
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Rigorous hydrostatic reduction of free fall: two bodies of identical material connected by a weightless thread fall at the same speed as either alone; velocity in vacuo would be finite and equal for all homogeneous bodies.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the scholastic paradox of connected falling bodies; enabled Stevin & De Groot (B1-017) to conduct tower drop tests and Galileo (B1-020) to frame De Motu.

Original Title & English Translation: Liber de centro gravitatis solidorum (Book on the Center of Gravity of Solids)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Bologna: Alessandro Benacci, 1558
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Geometrical derivation of centers of gravity of 3D solids (pyramids, cones, paraboloids of revolution); generalized Archimedean planar equilibrium to volumetric spatial distributions.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the spatial limitation of Archimedean planar statics; directly provided the mathematical apparatus for Guidobaldo del Monte's statics (B1-013) and Galileo's 1588 center-of-gravity theorems (B1-050 app.).

Original Title & English Translation: Archimedis De iis quae vehuntur in aqua libri duo (Archimedes' Two Books on Floating Bodies)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Bologna: Alessandro Benacci, 1565
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First complete Latin translation and rigorous mathematical commentary on Archimedes' hydrostatics, restoring stability proofs for submerged and floating paraboloids under angular tilt.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the corruption of medieval manuscript traditions of hydrostatics; directly equipped Stevin (B1-018) and Galileo (B1-032) to formulate modern hydrostatic mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Opus novum de proportionibus numerorum, motuum, ponderum, sonorum (New Work on the Proportions of Numbers, Motions, Weights, Sounds)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Basel: Henricus Petri, 1569
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Introduced dynamic mechanical advantage formulations; attempted quantitative functional relationships between motive power, resistance, angle of inclined plane, and velocity of discharge.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the isolation of kinematic problems from mathematical proportion theory; stimulated Stevin (B1-016) to establish static vector decompositions on inclined planes.

Original Title & English Translation: De Nova et nullius aevi memoria prius visa Stella (On the New and Never Previously Seen Star of November 1572)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Copenhagen: Laurentius Benedictus, 1573
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Diurnal parallax measurement of SN 1572 using sextants; proved parallax < 1 arcmin, placing the supernova unequivocally beyond the Moon within the sphere of fixed stars.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Aristotelian dogma of celestial immutability and incorruptibility; forced mathematical astronomers (Kepler B1-021, B1-028) to treat the heavens as a dynamic physical domain.

Original Title & English Translation: Arithmeticorum Libri Duo (Two Books of Arithmetic) & Photismi de lumine et umbra
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Venice: Francesco Franceschi, 1575
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formalized the principle of mathematical induction; derived summations of triangular numbers and squares; analyzed rectilinear propagation of light through pinhole apertures.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the proof bottleneck for infinite series sums of discrete moments; directly enabled Cavalieri (B1-047) to calculate geometric indivisibles and Kepler (B1-026) to formalize optical rays.

Original Title & English Translation: Dialogo intorno alla Meccanica (Dialogue Concerning Mechanics, Padua MS)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Padua: Manuscript, c. 1576 (Biblioteca Ambrosiana, Milan, MS S. 100 sup.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Experimental drop test from a high tower in Padua of equal-volume balls of lead and wood; demonstrated empirically that they reach the ground at the identical moment, anticipating Galileo's demonstration.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the lack of experimental verification in Aristotelian fall rates; established the Padua experimental tradition that directly instructed Galileo Galilei (B1-020).

Original Title & English Translation: A Perfit Description of the Caelestiall Orbes according to the most aunciente doctrine of the Pythagoreans, latelye revived by Copernicus and by Geometricall Demonstrations approved (A Perfect Description of the Celestial Orbs...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: Thomas Marsh, 1576 (appended to Leonard Digges' Prognostication everlastinge)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First explicit rejection of the Copernican outer crystalline sphere of fixed stars; replaced the bounded sphere with an infinitely extending physical Euclidean space populated with stars at varying radial distances; first diagram of an infinite, non-bounded heliocentric universe.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the spatial confinement bottleneck of Copernicus's finite eighth sphere (De revolutionibus B1-001); directly inspired Giordano Bruno (B1-052) to conceptualize an infinite plurality of worlds and removed the boundary condition for isotropic mechanical space.

Original Title & English Translation: Mechanicorum Liber (Book of Mechanics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Pesaro: Girolamo Concordia, 1577
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Rigorous reduction of all five classical simple machines (lever, wheel and axle, pulley, wedge, screw) to the Archimedean lever; eliminated dynamic impetus errors from equilibrium statics.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the scholastic confusion between static equilibrium and dynamic motion; directly instructed Galileo's Padova lectures Le Mecaniche (B1-022).

Original Title & English Translation: Experimental discovery of pendulum isochronism (Pisa Cathedral observations; recorded in Pisan manuscripts)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Pisa: MS notes, c. 1581 (later detailed in Discorsi, 1638)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Observed that a swinging pendulum has an oscillation period independent of arc amplitude for small oscillations; used pulse rate as an invariant physiological chronometer.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the lack of precision timekeeping instruments for dynamic intervals; provided the essential tool for timing accelerated motion (B1-024) and Mersenne's acoustic tests (B1-048).

Original Title & English Translation: La Cena de le Ceneri (The Ash Wednesday Supper), Dialogue III
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: John Charlewood, 1584 (8vo)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the classic thought experiment of the moving ship's mast: demonstrated that a stone dropped from the top of the mast of a ship in uniform motion falls straight down along the mast and lands at its base, sharing the ship's forward motion (impeto impresso), rather than lagging behind as Aristotelians claimed.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Aristotelian kinematic counter-argument against terrestrial rotation (which asserted dropping stones from towers would be left behind by the rotating Earth); directly anticipated and pre-structured Galileo's relativistic ship experiment in the Dialogo (B1-044).

Original Title & English Translation: Diversarum speculationum mathematicarum et physicarum liber (Book of Various Mathematical and Physical Speculations)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Turin: Bevilacqua, 1585
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated centrifugal rectilinear tendency: a stone whirled in a sling and released travels along the rectilinear tangent to the circle, not a curved radial trajectory; introduced air resistance as surface-dependent drag.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Aristotelian doctrine that circular motion is natural and self-sustaining; directly enabled Beeckman (B1-038), Descartes (B1-049), and Newton to isolate rectilinear inertia from centripetal restraint.

Original Title & English Translation: De Beghinselen der Weeghconst (The Elements of the Art of Weighing)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: Christoffel Plantijn (Jan Paedts), 1586
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proved the law of the inclined plane via the Clootcrans (wreath of spheres) perpetual motion impossibility proof: F1 / F2 = L1 / L2; formulated geometric vector triangle of forces in equilibrium.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the century-long erroneous dynamic balance equations of Jordanus de Nemore and Tartaglia; gave Galileo (B1-022) and Descartes the exact geometric resolution of inclined forces.

Scientist: Simon Stevin (1548–1620) & Jan Cornets de Groot (1554–1640)
Original Title & English Translation: Vande vrye comste der zwaerheden (On the Free Fall of Heavy Bodies, in Weeghconst)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: Christoffel Plantijn (Jan Paedts), 1586
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Dropped two lead spheres, one ten times heavier than the other, from 30 feet of height onto a wooden board from the church tower in Delft; reported simultaneous sound of impact, disproving Aristotle's 10:1 speed ratio.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the empirical dispute over fall velocities through air; served as the printed milestone of empirical disproof of Aristotle prior to Galileo's Discorsi (B1-050).

Original Title & English Translation: De Beghinselen des Waterwichts (The Elements of Hydrostatics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: Christoffel Plantijn (Jan Paedts), 1586
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Discovered the Hydrostatic Paradox: bottom pressure of a liquid column depends exclusively on vertical height h and base area A, completely independent of the vessel's geometric shape or total water volume (P = rho * g * h).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the total-weight confusion in fluid pressure; enabled Pascal's principle of hydraulic multiplication (1654) and Mersenne's fluid mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: De Mundi Aetherei Recentioribus Phaenomenis Liber Secundus (Second Book on More Recent Phenomena of the Aethereal World)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Uraniborg: Typis Authoris, 1588
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Triangulated the Great Comet of 1577; proved comet passed through interplanetary space across the planetary orbits; formulated the geo-heliocentric Tychonic planetary model; physically dissolved crystalline spheres into fluid ether.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the celestial collision problem of intersecting orbits; freed Kepler (B1-028) from rigid mechanical spheres to propose dynamic orbital trajectories through open space.

Original Title & English Translation: De Motu Antiquiora (Older Writings on Motion)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Pisa: Manuscript treatises, c. 1590 (BNCF MS Gal. 71)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Modeled descent on inclined planes as diluted gravity; analyzed motion through resistive media via buoyancy imbalance; argued acceleration at the start of fall is an overcoming of remnant adverse impetus.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the disconnection between free fall and inclined plane constraint; established the conceptual laboratory that led directly to Galileo's s proportional to t^2 law (B1-025).

Original Title & English Translation: Prodromus Dissertationum Cosmographicarum, continens Mysterium Cosmographicum (The Cosmographic Mystery)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Tübingen: Georg Gruppenbach, 1596
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Modeled planetary orbital spacing via nested Platonic solids; proposed for the first time a centralized physical motive soul/force (anima motrix) residing in the Sun, weakening with distance, that drives the planets.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the kinematic arbitrariness of Copernican orbital spheres; inaugurated the physical search for dynamic celestial mechanics culminating in Astronomia Nova (B1-028).

Original Title & English Translation: Le Mecaniche (Mechanics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Padua: MS lecture notes, 1597–1600 (printed by Mersenne, Paris 1634; Ravenna, 1649)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Unified the balance, lever, windlass, screw, and inclined plane under the Principle of Virtual Displacements: motive power is inversely proportional to the displacement/speed along the line of gravity (F * delta_s = W * delta_h).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the fragmented operational treatment of simple machines; laid the virtual work foundation used by Wallis, Huygens, and Lagrange (1788).

Original Title & English Translation: De Magnete, Magneticisque Corporibus, et de Magno Magnete Tellure (On the Magnet and Magnetic Bodies)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: Peter Short, 1600 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proved the Earth is a dipolar permanent magnet using spherical lodestone (terrella); demonstrated non-contact action at a distance (orbis virtutis); linked planetary diurnal rotation to intrinsic magnetic rotation.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the metaphysical barrier to action-at-a-distance immaterial forces; directly inspired Kepler (B1-028) to substitute magnetic filaments for the solar anima motrix.

Original Title & English Translation: De Reflexione et Refractione & De Motu Ballistico (Manuscript folios on Refraction and Projectile Trajectories)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: Manuscript folios, c. 1601–1603 (British Library, Add MS 6788 & Add MS 6789; Petworth House HMC 241/vi)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Discovered mathematically the sine law of refraction in July 1601 (predating Snellius by 20 years and Descartes by 36 years); calculated projectile trajectories as exact parabolas compounded of uniform horizontal velocity and accelerating descent (c. 1601–1603), computing ballistic tables for cannon elevation angles.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved Tartaglia's approximate curved ballistic paths (B1-003) and empirical refraction tables; independently provided the exact mathematical trajectory of projectiles and sine law of refraction prior to Galileo's Discorsi (B1-050) and Snellius (B1-040).

Original Title & English Translation: Lettera a Guidobaldo del Monte (Letter to Guidobaldo del Monte on Pendulum Motion and Chords of a Circle)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Padua: Letter, 29 Nov 1602 (Opere, Ed. Naz. X, pp. 97–100)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Geometrical proof of the Chord Theorem: time of descent along any chord of a vertical circle terminating at the lowest point (or originating from the highest point) is identical and equal to the time of free fall along the diameter.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the quantitative comparison between straight inclined descents and curved circular swings; enabled Galileo to formulate brachistochrone conjectures and Huygens to discover the cycloid (1659).

Original Title & English Translation: Ad Vitellionem Paralipomena, quibus Astronomiae Pars Optica Traditur (Optical Part of Astronomy)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Frankfurt: Claude de Marne & heirs of Aubry, 1604
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Derived the inverse-square law for the propagation of light intensity: I proportional to 1/r^2 based on expanding spherical wavefront areas; developed geometric ray tracing and optical refraction corrections for celestial altitudes.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the optical distortion bottleneck in astronomical coordinate measurements; provided the geometric prototype for central inverse-square physical forces later adopted by Newton (1687).

Original Title & English Translation: Lettera a Fra Paolo Sarpi (Letter to Paolo Sarpi on the Law of Free Fall)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Padua: Letter, 16 Oct 1604 (Opere, Ed. Naz. X, pp. 115–116)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First written formulation of the times-squared law: distance fallen is proportional to the square of elapsed time (s proportional to t^2); derived the sequence of odd numbers (1, 3, 5, 7...) for distances traversed in successive equal time intervals.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the mathematical expression of acceleration from rest; though initially misattributing v proportional to s, it directly spurred the correct deduction v proportional to t in Discorsi (B1-050).

Original Title & English Translation: Wisconstighe Ghedachtenissen / Hypomnemata Mathematica (Mathematical Memoirs)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: Jan Bouwensz, 1605–1608
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Expanded static force equilibrium to 3D spatial systems; systematized center of gravity algorithms using continuous infinitesimal slice limits; integrated navigational loxodromes with kinematics.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the planar constraint of Stevin's 1586 statics; provided Cavalieri (B1-047) and Descartes with foundations for analytical coordinate geometry and mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Astronomia Nova AITIOLOGETOS, seu Physica Coelestis (New Astronomy Based on Causes, or Celestial Physics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Prague / Heidelberg: Gotthard Vögelin, 1609 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Discovered Kepler's First Law (Mars moves in an ellipse with the Sun at one focus) and Second Law (radius vector sweeps out equal areas in equal times: dA/dt = const); defined physical inertia as resistance to motion.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the 2000-year circular orbit dogma and the failure of Brahe's Mars data; established the kinematic laws that Newton's inverse-square dynamics (1687) was created to explain.

Original Title & English Translation: Observationes astronomicae per telescopium: Carta selenographica (Astronomical Observations through a Telescope: Lunar Drawings)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Syon House, Isleworth: MS records, 26 July 1609 (Petworth House Archives, HMC 241/ix; preserved in West Sussex Record Office)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Conducted the first recorded telescopic astronomical observation and produced the earliest topographic drawing of the Moon through a 6x perspective tube on 26 July 1609 (Old Style), four months before Galileo's first lunar telescopic observation in November 1609.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the technical application of the Dutch spyglass to celestial coordinate geometry; established the British empirical observational tradition that preceded and corroborated Galileo's Sidereus Nuncius (B1-029).

Original Title & English Translation: Sidereus Nuncius (The Starry Messenger)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Venice: Tommaso Baglioni, 1610
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Telescopic discovery of the four Medicean satellites (moons) of Jupiter; measured their orbital periods; resolved the lunar surface into mountainous craters; proved Earth is not the unique center of orbital motion.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the kinematic objection that Earth cannot move through space without losing its Moon; provided empirical verification of Copernican celestial mechanics (B1-001).

Original Title & English Translation: Dioptrice (Dioptrics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Augsburg: David Francke, 1611
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the geometrical optics of the Keplerian astronomical telescope using two convex lenses (objective + ocular); derived image magnification and focal length equations (1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i for thin lenses).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the narrow field-of-view and low magnification limitations of the Galilean concave eyepiece; enabled precision micrometer measurements in celestial kinematics (Horrocks, Cassini).

Original Title & English Translation: De Maculis in Sole Observatis, et Apparente earum cum Sole Conversione Narratio (Narration on Spots Observed on the Sun)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Wittenberg: Laurentius Seuberlich, 1611
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First printed announcement of sunspots observed via camera obscura; tracked spot displacement across the solar disc, proving uniform axial rotation of the Sun itself with an ~27-day period.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the problem of whether celestial bodies exhibit intrinsic spin; provided physical proof of Kepler's hypothesis (B1-021) that the rotating Sun acts as a physical kinematic dynamo.

Original Title & English Translation: Discorso intorno alle cose che stanno in su l'acqua, o che in quella si muovono (Discourse on Floating Bodies)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Florence: Cosimo Giunti, 1612
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proved that floating and sinking depend entirely on the ratio of specific gravities of solid and fluid (Archimedes) combined with the principle of virtual velocities; refuted Aristotelian shape-based flotation.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Aristotelian scholastic objection regarding surface tension and shape in equilibrium; extended the virtual work principle of Le Mecaniche (B1-022) to fluid mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Istoria e dimostrazioni intorno alle macchie solari e loro accidenti (Letters on Sunspots)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Rome: Giacomo Mascardi, 1613
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proved sunspots reside on or immediately contiguous to the solar surface; formulated the first explicit statement of conservation of circular motion on a frictionless sphere: motion once imparted persists indefinitely without attenuation.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved Scheiner's erroneous model of intra-Mercurial planets; established the precursor concept to uniform rectilinear inertia formalized by Beeckman (B1-038) and Descartes (B1-049).

Original Title & English Translation: Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio (Description of the Admirable Table of Logarithms)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Edinburgh: Andrew Hart, 1614
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Invented logarithms based on the kinematic comparison of two moving points: one moving with uniform velocity and one with velocity proportional to remaining distance; converted multi-digit multiplication into addition.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the immense computational bottleneck of multi-digit trigonometric operations in celestial kinematics; directly enabled Kepler to calculate the Rudolphine Tables (B1-043).

Original Title & English Translation: Nova Stereometria Doliorum Vinariorum (New Solid Geometry of Wine Casks)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Linz: Johannes Plancus, 1615 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Calculated volumes of solids of revolution by summing an infinite number of infinitely small (indivisible) elements; discovered that near a maximum, the rate of change of a geometric quantity vanishes (delta_V approx 0).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Archimedean exhaustion bottleneck for non-standard volumes; directly founded Cavalieri's method of indivisibles (B1-047) and Fermat's method of maxima and minima (1636).

Original Title & English Translation: Eratosthenes Batavus: De terrae ambitus vera quantitate (Eratosthenes the Batavian: On the True Size of the Earth's Circumference)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: Jodocus van Colster, 1617 (4to)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Invented the method of geodetic triangulation using a network of 33 triangles between Alkmaar and Bergen op Zoom to measure a 1-degree meridian arc; calculated Earth's circumference to within ~3.5% accuracy (107.395 km per degree vs actual 111.3 km); laid the foundation for spatial geodesy.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the crude odometer/pacing error bottleneck of antiquity and medieval geodesy; provided the precise terrestrial linear radius and curvature measurements that Jean Picard (1671) and Newton (1687) required to confirm inverse-square gravitational acceleration between Earth and Moon.

Original Title & English Translation: Epitome Astronomiae Copernicanae (Epitome of Copernican Astronomy, Books I–VII)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Linz & Frankfurt: Gottfried Tambach / Johann Plancus, 1618, 1620, 1621
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Generalized Kepler's Three Laws to all planets and planetary satellites; formulated physical celestial mechanics: planetary velocities decrease with distance due to weakening of the rotating solar magnetic rays.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the isolated single-planet solution of Astronomia Nova; served as the primary textbook of heliocentric elliptical mechanics that educated Horrocks, Gassendi, and Newton.

Original Title & English Translation: Journal tenu par Isaac Beeckman de 1604 à 1634 (Notebook entries on mechanics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Middelburg: MS Journal (Royal Library, The Hague, MS 74 B 27)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated clear mechanical law of rectilinear inertia: a body in motion in a vacuum continues to move in a straight line at constant speed indefinitely (omne quod movetur pergit movere quamdiu non impeditur); deduced v proportional to t in fall.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the medieval impetus decay misconception; communicated rectilinear inertia directly to Descartes in Breda (1618–1619), who incorporated it into Le Monde and Discours (B1-049).

Original Title & English Translation: Harmonices Mundi Libri V (The Harmony of the World, in Five Books)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Linz: Gottfried Tambach (typis Johannis Planci), 1619
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Discovered Kepler's Third Law (Harmonic Law): the squares of the orbital periods of the planets are directly proportional to the cubes of their semi-major axes (P^2 proportional to a^3 or T^2 / a^3 = const).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the absence of a unified kinematic scaling law across the planetary system; provided the mathematical constraint that enabled Newton (1684) to deduce the 1/r^2 central gravitational force law.

Original Title & English Translation: Novum Organum Scientiarum (New Instrument of Science), Part II of Instauratio Magna
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: John Bill, 1620
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Established the inductive method based on systematic tables of presence, absence, and degrees; insisted on mechanical operationalism and empirical verification over scholastic syllogism.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the deductive stasis of scholastic natural philosophy; became the philosophical manifesto for empirical academy experimentation (Royal Society, Academie des Sciences).

Original Title & English Translation: Manuscript derivation of the Law of Refraction
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: MS notes, c. 1621 (preserved in Isaac Vossius & Huygens MSS)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the exact trigonometric law of refraction: ratio of cosecants of angle of incidence and angle of refraction is constant (csc theta_1 / csc theta_2 = const, mathematically equivalent to sin theta_1 / sin theta_2 = n).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved Ptolemy's and Witelo's empirical approximation tables for refraction; provided Descartes (B1-049) and Fermat the mathematical foundation for ray optics and variational Fermat's Principle (1662).

Original Title & English Translation: Il Saggiatore (The Assayer)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Rome: Giacomo Mascardi, 1623
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proclaimed that the universe is written in mathematical characters (triangles, circles, and geometric figures); demarcated primary quantifiable physical properties (size, shape, quantity, motion) from subjective secondary qualities.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the qualitative scholastic metaphysics of essences and forms; established mathematical modeling as the mandatory language of classical mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Arithmetica Logarithmica (Logarithmic Arithmetic)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: William Jones, 1624 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Computed and published 14-decimal-place tables of common logarithms (base 10: log10) for the natural numbers 1 to 20,000 and 90,000 to 100,000; introduced methods of finite differences for numerical interpolation.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the awkward non-decimal conversion ratios of Napier's logarithms; provided Kepler and European astronomers with the definitive computational tables for high-precision celestial kinematics.

Original Title & English Translation: Tabulae Rudolphinae (Rudolphine Tables)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Ulm: Jonas Saur, 1627 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First comprehensive astronomical tables based entirely on elliptical heliocentric orbits with areal velocity invariance; reduced planetary prediction errors from multiple degrees to under a few arcminutes.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the chronic cumulative positional errors of Reinhold's Prussian Tables; allowed Kepler to accurately predict the 1631 transits of Mercury and Venus, verified by Gassendi (B1-045).

Original Title & English Translation: Mercurius in Sole Visus, et Venus Invisa Anno 1631 (Mercury Seen in the Sun, and Venus Not Seen in 1631)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Sebastien Cramoisy, 1632

Original Title & English Translation: Mathematical Invention of the Infinitesimal Calculus (Operational Notation)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Manuscript notes, 11 Nov 1675 (Leibniz Archives, Hannover, LH 35, II, 1, Bl. 1–4)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the modern operational notation of the differential and integral calculus: introduced the integral sign (long S for summa) and the differential dx; derived the fundamental integration rule integral x dx = x^2 / 2 and the inverse property d(integral y dx) = y dx.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the clumsy geometric and verbal representations of infinitesimal sums; established the algebraic symbolic algorithm that made analytical mechanics possible for the Bernoullis, Euler, and Lagrange.

Original Title & English Translation: Démonstration touchant le mouvement de la lumière trouvé par M. Römer (Demonstration Concerning the Motion of Light)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Journal des Sçavans, 7 Dec 1676, pp. 233–236; Philosophical Transactions, Vol. 12, No. 136, 1677, pp. 893–894
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Proved light propagates with a finite velocity by analyzing orbital timing anomalies in the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io: eclipses occurred 22 minutes later when Earth was farthest from Jupiter; calculated finite velocity c approx 220,000 km/s.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the ancient and Cartesian axiom that light propagates instantaneously (c = inf); transformed optical physics into a time-dependent mechanical transmission process.

Original Title & English Translation: Traité de la percussion ou chocq des corps (Treatise on the Percussion or Impact of Bodies)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Estienne Michallet, 1677 (12mo)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Conducted extensive pendulum collision experiments using suspended spheres of diverse materials (ivory, glass, lead, wood); introduced the quantitative coefficient of restitution e = |v1 - v2| / |u1 - u2|; separated perfectly elastic from inelastic behavior.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the lack of material-dependent empirical parameters in Wren's and Huygens' idealized elastic collision laws; provided the verified empirical collision datasets cited by Newton in the Principia.

Original Title & English Translation: Lectures De Potentia Restitutiva, or Of Spring Explaining the Power of Springing Bodies
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: John Martyn, 1678 (4to)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Decrypted his 1676 anagram ceiiinosssttuv into the fundamental law of elasticity: Ut tensio, sic vis ('As the extension, so the force', F = kx); calculated the potential energy stored in an extended spring as the triangular area beneath the force-extension line (W = 0.5 * k * x^2).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the undefined mathematical relation between restoring force and deformation; provided the linear spring potential that enabled Newton and Euler to model harmonic oscillators.

Original Title & English Translation: Pivotal Correspondence on Celestial Planetary Mechanics (Letters of Nov 1679 – Jan 1680)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London & Cambridge: Holograph letters (Hooke to Newton 24 Nov 1679, 6 Jan 1680; Newton to Hooke 13 Dec 1679)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Hooke instructed Newton to abandon spiral paths and model planetary orbits by compounding an inertial tangential motion with a central attractive force varying inversely as the square of the distance (F proportional to 1/r^2); Newton calculated orbital curves under central force.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved Newton's erroneous spiral trajectory misconception of falling bodies on a rotating Earth; served as the direct catalyst that prompted Newton to calculate the Keplerian elliptical orbit under inverse-square forces.

Original Title & English Translation: Observations sur la Comète de 1680 et 1681 (Observations on the Great Comet of 1680)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Académie Royale des Sciences, 1681 & Philosophical Transactions, 1681
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Tracked the trajectory of the Great Comet of 1680; proved it was a single continuous body executing a tight perihelion hairpin turn around the Sun, rather than two separate comets travelling in straight lines.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Aristotelian and Keplerian doctrine that comets travel in straight rectilinear paths through the solar system; provided Newton with the crucial observational dataset to prove comets obey conic orbits under universal gravitation.

Original Title & English Translation: De Motu Animalium (On the Movement of Animals), 2 vols.
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Rome: Typographia Angeli Bernabò, 1680–1681 (4to)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Founded biomechanics: modeled human and animal musculoskeletal movement through rigid Archimedean levers, geometric vector force resolutions, muscle tension calculations, center-of-gravity balancing, and fluid hydrodynamic drag in avian and aquatic locomotion.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the metaphysical vitalist barrier in physiology; unified living organism kinematics under the identical mechanical laws governing inanimate machines.

Original Title & English Translation: Astronomical Observations and Orbital Calculations of the Great Comet of 1682
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Greenwich & London: Royal Society MS records, Aug–Sept 1682
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Tracked the coordinates and nodal crossings of the Comet of 1682; compiled historical comet apparitions that later formed the basis for Halley's 1705 Synopsis Astronomiae Cometicae predicting its 76-year periodic return.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the classification of comets as random, non-periodic wanderers; provided the empirical bedrock proving that cometary motions belong to closed, eccentric gravitational orbits.

Scientist: Edmond Halley (1656–1742), Christopher Wren (1632–1723), Robert Hooke (1635–1703)
Original Title & English Translation: The Royal Society Coffee House Challenge and Halley's Visit to Cambridge
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London & Cambridge: Royal Society Council Minutes & historical accounts (Aug 1684)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Wren offered a prize of a book worth 40 shillings to anyone who could demonstrate mathematically what orbit an inverse-square force produces; Halley traveled to Cambridge and posed the question to Newton, who replied immediately: 'an Ellipsis'.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the communication paralysis among London natural philosophers unable to solve the inverse Kepler problem; provoked Newton to produce the foundational tract De Motu Corporum in Gyrum (B2-049).

Original Title & English Translation: Nova Methodus pro Maximis et Minimis, itemque tangentibus... (A New Method for Maxima and Minima, as well as Tangents...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Oct 1684, pp. 467–473
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First published paper on the differential calculus: introduced rules for differentials of powers, products d(uv) = u dv + v du, and quotients; established algorithmic conditions for extrema (dy = 0) and points of inflection (d^2y = 0).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the cumbersome geometric tangent methods of Barrow and Descartes; provided European continental mathematicians with the explicit analytical differential apparatus used to reformulate Newtonian mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: De motu corporum in gyrum (On the Motion of Bodies in an Orbit)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Cambridge: Holograph tract sent to Royal Society, registered Nov–Dec 1684 (Register Book of the Royal Society, Vol. VI, pp. 218–234)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): The foundational 9-page tract of modern dynamics: derived Kepler's Second Law for any central force; demonstrated geometrically that an elliptical orbit implies an inverse-square centripetal force (F proportional to 1/r^2); coined the term vis centripeta.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the inverse-square orbit problem posed by Halley and Hooke; directly expanded over the next two years into the three books of the Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (B2-055).

Original Title & English Translation: Brevis Demonstratio Erroris Memorabilis Cartesii... (Brief Demonstration of the Notable Error of Descartes...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, March 1686, pp. 161–163
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Inaugurated the Vis Viva controversy: proved mathematically that Descartes' scalar quantity of motion (sum m|v|) is not conserved; using Galileo's fall law (h proportional to v^2), proved true motive force is measured by mass times the square of velocity (m*v^2, vis viva).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the false conservation law of Cartesian mechanics; initiated the fundamental 60-year mechanical debate over momentum vs. kinetic energy conservation resolved by d'Alembert (1743).

Original Title & English Translation: A Discourse Concerning Gravity, and Its Properties
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: Philosophical Transactions, Vol. 16, No. 179, June 1686, pp. 3–21
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Comprehensive mathematical synthesis of terrestrial Galilean acceleration, ballistic parabolas in non-resisting media, pendulum periods, and celestial inverse-square gravitational forces; explicitly announced Newton's forthcoming Principia.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the public dissemination gap between experimental ballistics and celestial central forces; prepared the scientific community for the Newtonian mathematical synthesis.

Original Title & English Translation: Traité du mouvement des eaux et des autres corps fluides (Treatise on the Motion of Water and Other Fluid Bodies)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Estienne Michallet, 1686 (8vo)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Quantitative experimental hydrodynamics: measured velocity profiles of water jets, discharge rates through pipes as a function of head height and friction (v proportional to sqrt(h)); analyzed dynamic pressure and aerodynamic drag on moving plates.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the idealization of fluid efflux that ignored wall friction and viscosity; provided the empirical fluid resistance benchmarks analyzed by Newton in Book II of the Principia.

Original Title & English Translation: Projet d'une nouvelle mechanique (Project for a New Mechanics)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Veuve d'Edme Martin, 1687 (4to)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the Parallelogram of Forces and Varignon's Theorem: the torque of the resultant force about any point equals the algebraic sum of the torques of the individual concurrent component forces (tau_R = sum tau_i); unified static equilibrium via moments.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the cumbersome geometric resolutions of concurrent and non-concurrent mechanical forces; established the vector-moment equilibrium method that became standard throughout engineering statics.

Original Title & English Translation: Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: Jussu Societatis Regiae ac Typis Josephi Streater, prostant venales apud Sam. Smith, 1687 (4to)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): The master synthesis of classical physics: Definitions of mass, momentum, inertia, and centripetal force; Three Laws of Motion (F = dot{p}, action-reaction); Book I: motion under central forces in vacuo (conic orbits, Kepler's laws); Book II: motion in resisting fluids (v, v^2), speed of sound (c = sqrt(P/rho)), mathematical refutation of Cartesian vortices; Book III: System of the World, Law of Universal Gravitation (F = G*m1*m2/r^2), quantitative theory of tides, lunar inequalities, planetary masses, oblate planetary figures, and parabolic cometary orbits.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the total disjunction between terrestrial kinematics and celestial mechanics; concluded Batch 2 and established the foundational paradigm of physical law that governed all science through the 18th and 19th centuries.

Original Title & English Translation: Schediasma de resistentia medii, & motu projectorum gravium in medio resistente (Essay on the Resistance of the Medium, and Motion of Heavy Projectiles in a Resisting Medium)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Jan 1689, pp. 38–47
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated differential equations for projectile motion under gravity with air resistance proportional to velocity (R proportional to v); separated horizontal and vertical variables via logarithmic differentials: dx = v0 dt / (1 + c*t).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the geometric tractability bottleneck of Newton's resisting medium propositions in Book II of Principia (B2-055); directly enabled Varignon (B3-016) and Euler (B3-045) to integrate complex resistance laws.

Original Title & English Translation: Tentamen de motuum coelestium causis (Essay on the Causes of Celestial Motions)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Feb 1689, pp. 82–96
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated differential equations for central orbital motion by decomposing radial and transverse velocities; introduced the harmonic circulation condition r^2 * (dtheta/dt) = C and radial differential acceleration d^2 r = (C^2/r^3 - k/r^2)*dt^2.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the geometric synthetic barrier of Newton's central force proofs; provided Jakob Hermann (B3-028) and Johann Bernoulli (B3-029) with the explicit radial differential equation of planetary orbits.

Original Title & English Translation: Traité de la lumière (Treatise on Light)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leiden: Pieter van der Aa, 1690 (completed 1678)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated Huygens' Principle: every point on a propagating wavefront acts as the source of secondary spherical wavelets; derived the wave laws of reflection, refraction, and extraordinary refraction in uniaxial calcite crystals via ellipsoidal wave envelopes.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the failure of corpuscular mechanics to explain double refraction (B2-033); established the continuum wave mechanics that Fresnel, Young, and Maxwell later mathematized.

Original Title & English Translation: Analysis problematis antehac propositi, de motu corporum gravium in fune... (Analysis of a Proposed Problem on the Motion of Heavy Bodies...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1690, pp. 217–219
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Solved Leibniz's Isochrone Problem (the curve of uniform vertical descent): derived the differential equation dy * sqrt(y) = a * sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2), identifying the curve as the semi-cubical parabola; introduced for the first time in mathematical history the word integral (integral sign).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the ancient problem of curves of uniform vertical kinematic action; established the term and foundational operational method of integral calculus in dynamic mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Nouvelle manière de produire de très grandes forces à bon marché (A New Way of Producing Immense Forces Cheaply)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Aug 1690, pp. 410–414
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Invented the atmospheric piston-cylinder steam engine: generated a vacuum beneath a piston by condensing steam inside a cylinder, utilizing external atmospheric pressure to drive the piston downward and generate mechanical work.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the unreliability and hazard of gunpowder-driven mechanical cylinders; created the thermodynamic operational cycle that Newcomen (B3-032) and Watt industrialized into the motive force of mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematis funicularii, exhibita a Jacobo Bernoulli (Solution of the Catenary Problem...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, June 1691, pp. 274–276
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the differential equation of equilibrium for a flexible, inextensible hanging chain under gravity: balance of horizontal tension and vertical weight yields dy = (s*dx)/a; integrated the equation to discover the catenary curve (y = a * cosh(x/a)).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved Galileo's erroneous conjecture in the Discorsi (B1-050) that a hanging cord forms a parabola; established the static equilibrium differential equations for flexible continuum media.

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematis de linea catenaria (Solution of the Problem of the Catenary Line)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, June 1691, pp. 277–281
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Independently solved the catenary using a characteristic force-triangle of infinitesimal cable segments: derived dx = a*dy / sqrt(y^2 - a^2), integrating to the logarithmic form equivalent to the hyperbolic cosine; demonstrated that the catenary evolute is a tractrix.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the static indeterminacy of flexible cables; launched Johann Bernoulli's international reputation and established his differential technique for mechanical curves.

Original Title & English Translation: De linea in quam flexile grave si pondere suo incurvetur... Catenaria (On the Line Formed by a Heavy Flexible Chain...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, June 1691, pp. 277–282
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Published Leibniz's independent solution of the catenary using the exponential/logarithmic relation between coordinates: y = (a/2)*(e^(x/a) + e^(-x/a)); proved that the center of gravity of the catenary is lower than that of any other curve of equal length.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the analytical representation of transcendental curves in mechanics; directly anticipated the variational principle of minimal potential energy for static equilibrium.

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematis de curvis elasticis, velariis et linteariis (Solution of Problems of Elastic, Velaria, and Lintearia Curves)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, 1692–1695
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the differential equations of the Velaria (curve assumed by a sail inflated by wind pressure, d^2y/dx^2 proportional to normal pressure) and Lintearia (profile of a flexible container holding water, where pressure is proportional to depth).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the coupling of fluid hydrostatic pressure fields to flexible structural boundaries; established the differential boundary equations foundational to aero- and hydro-elasticity.

Original Title & English Translation: Specimen alterum calculi differentialis... de motu corporum gravium (Another Specimen of Differential Calculus... on the Motion of Heavy Bodies)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Dec 1692, pp. 498–507
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Derived the universal intrinsic differential formula for the radius of curvature of any plane curve: rho = ds^3 / (dx * d^2y - dy * d^2x) (or rho = [1 + (y')^2]^(3/2) / y''); applied it to the normal acceleration of particles traversing mechanical trajectories.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the geometric construction bottleneck of Huygens' evolutes (B2-038); provided the foundational mathematical operator for normal acceleration (a_n = v^2/rho) across analytical mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Mathematical Correspondence on the Tractrix and Centrifugal Force
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris & The Hague: Letters published in Journal des Sçavans, Feb 1693 & Sept 1693
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Solved the Tractrix (curve of pursuit along a rough surface under constant pulling lead): derived the differential equation dy/dx = -sqrt(a^2 - x^2)/x; proved that the tractrix is the involute of the catenary and possesses a constant tangent segment length.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the kinematic formulation of dry friction constraints; laid the groundwork for non-holonomic mechanics and differential pursuit geometries.

Original Title & English Translation: Curvatura Laminae Elasticae & Constructio Curvae accessus et recessus aequabilis (Curvature of an Elastic Lamina...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Sept 1694, pp. 262–276
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Derived the differential equation of the Lemniscate of Bernoulli ((x^2+y^2)^2 = 2*a^2*(x^2-y^2)); integrated the arc length using the differential form ds = (a^2 * dr) / sqrt(a^4 - r^4), introducing the very first elliptic integral in mathematical physics.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the non-elementary integration barrier for large-deflection elastic beams and nonlinear pendulums; opened the mathematical domain of elliptic functions later completed by Euler, Legendre, and Jacobi.

Original Title & English Translation: Opera Mathematica, Vols. I–II
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Oxford: The Sheldonian Theatre, 1693–1695 (fol.)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First comprehensive publication of Newton's method of fluxions (dot{x}, ddot{x}) in print; systematic integration of mechanical differential moments and centers of oscillation; defended British calculus priority.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the private unpublished circulation bottleneck of Newton's 1666 fluxion papers (B2-025); made the operational rules of fluxional mechanics publicly available across Britain.

Original Title & English Translation: Specimen Dynamicum pro admirandis naturae legibus... aperiendis (A Specimen of Dynamics for Uncovering the Admirable Laws of Nature...)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, April 1695, pp. 145–157
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Systematized the science of Dynamics: defined vis mortua (dead force, static pressure, tension, m * dv) versus vis viva (living force, kinetic energy, m * v^2); proved that under elastic interactions, total vis viva is conserved (sum m_i * v_i^2 = const); integrated integral F ds = 0.5 * m * v^2.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the conceptual confusion between static force (F) and dynamic capacity to do work; provided the mechanical and energetic foundation used by Johann Bernoulli (B3-038) and Emilie du Châtelet.

Original Title & English Translation: Analyse des infiniment petits pour l'intelligence des lignes courbes (Analysis of the Infinitely Small for Understanding Curved Lines)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Imprimerie Royale, 1696 (4to)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First published differential calculus textbook (codifying Johann Bernoulli's private lessons); formulated L'Hôpital's Rule for evaluating indeterminate differential ratios (lim f(x)/g(x) = f'(x)/g'(x) when 0/0); calculated evolutes, envelopes, and caustics.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the steep pedagogical barrier to Leibnizian calculus across France and the continent; trained the generation of Varignon, Maupertuis, and Clairaut in differential methods.

Original Title & English Translation: Problema novum, ad cujus solutionem Mathematici invitantur (A New Problem to Whose Solution Mathematicians Are Invited)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, June 1696, p. 269
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the Brachistochrone Challenge: determine the curve connecting two points A and B at different heights along which a heavy particle descending under gravity traverses the distance in the minimum possible time (t = integral ds / sqrt(2gy) = min).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the complacency of post-Newtonian mathematics by shifting from static point-extrema (df = 0) to functional extrema (finding an entire curve that optimizes an integral); directly launched the Calculus of Variations.

Original Title & English Translation: Lettre de M. Bernoulli à l'Auteur touchant son problême de la ligne de plus vîte descente
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Rotterdam: Histoire des Ouvrages des Sçavans, Nov–Dec 1696, pp. 455–458
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Extended the competition deadline from six months to Easter 1697 to ensure foreign mathematicians—explicitly targeting Newton in England and Varignon in France—had sufficient time to attempt the challenge.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the insular distribution bottleneck of German and Swiss mathematical journals; transformed a local challenge into a pan-European competition that engaged Newton, Leibniz, and L'Hôpital.

Original Title & English Translation: Epistola ad D. Carolum Mountague... qua exhibetur Solutio duorum Problematum Mathematicorum
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: London: Philosophical Transactions, Vol. 19, No. 224, Jan 1697, pp. 384–389 (received anonymously 29 Jan 1697)
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Solved the Brachistochrone anonymously overnight via the method of fluxions: proved the curve of fastest descent is an inverted cycloid; simultaneously solved the Solid of Least Resistance (finding the solid of revolution that experiences minimum resistance in a resisting fluid).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the foreign perception that English fluxional mathematics could not solve modern dynamic extremum problems; famously recognized by Johann Bernoulli: ex ungue leonem ('we recognize the lion by his claw').

Original Title & English Translation: Curvatura radii in diaphragmatibus... exhibita a Johanne Bernoulli (Curvature of a Ray in Diaphragms... Solution of the Brachistochrone)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1697, pp. 206–211
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Developed the celebrated optical-mechanical analogy: mapped a falling heavy particle to a light ray traversing a medium with variable refractive index n(y) proportional to 1/v = 1/sqrt(2gy); applied Fermat's Principle of Least Time (delta integral n ds = 0) and Snell's Law (sin alpha / v = const) to yield the cycloid differential equation: dx / sqrt(y(2a-y)) = dy / y.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the analytical intractability of the time functional; established the first profound formal equivalence between particle mechanics and wave optics (later revived by Hamilton in 1834).

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematum fraternorum... cum nova de problemate isoperimetrico propositione
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1697, pp. 211–217
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Solved the brachistochrone via intrinsic geometric variations: varied the position of an intermediate point while keeping flanking points fixed; derived the differential equation of the cycloid; introduced the Isoperimetric Problem: find the curve of given perimeter that maximizes bounded area or another integral functional.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the single-point variation limitation; initiated the study of constrained variational problems where one integral must be extremized while another remains constant.

Original Title & English Translation: Communicatio suae pariter, ac viri nobilissimi D. G. G. L. solutionis problematis de curva celerrimi descensus
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1697, pp. 201–205
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Solved the brachistochrone using the differential calculus of variations: varied ordinate increments dx, dy; demonstrated that the cycloid is uniquely both the Tautochrone (Huygens B2-017) and the Brachistochrone; emphasized the philosophical harmony of nature.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the disparate classification of mechanical curves; proved that the curve of equal descent time and the curve of least descent time are identical.

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematis de linea celerrimi descensus (Solution of the Problem of the Line of Quickest Descent)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1697, pp. 217–218
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Delivered an independent analytical differential solution of the brachistochrone using the calculus of infinitesimals: set the differential traversal time across adjacent segments equal to zero (dt1 + dt2 = 0), deriving the differential equation of the cycloid.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the Paris Académie's dependency on the Basel mathematicians; established the pedagogical template for variational minimization in French textbooks.

Original Title & English Translation: De curvis celerrimi descensus (On the Curves of Quickest Descent)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1697, p. 218
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Attempted an algebraic solution of the brachistochrone; analyzed the caustic and evolute properties of the cycloid in relation to mechanical descent.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the integration of catacaustic geometries with kinematics; stimulated Jakob Bernoulli's rigorous critique of non-infinitesimal approaches.

Original Title & English Translation: De motu gravium super curvata curva... Brachystochrona generalior
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, Dec 1697, pp. 560–565
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Generalized the brachistochrone: calculated the curve of fastest descent when the particle has an initial velocity v0 > 0 (yielding a cycloid originating above the starting line) and when the gravitational field is directed toward a fixed center of force (F proportional to 1/r^2).
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the uniform-field restriction (g = const) of the original problem; opened the field of central force variational paths.

Original Title & English Translation: Application de la méthode plénière pour les mouvemens quelconques à tous ceux qui arrivent par des forces centrales
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Histoire et Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences, Année 1698 (pub. 1700), pp. 220–243
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): First rigorous translation of Newton's verbal and geometric force into formal differential equations: explicitly defined instantaneous velocity as v = dx/dt and acceleration/force as y = dv/dt = d^2x/dt^2 (setting m=1); integrated equations of rectilinearly accelerated motion.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the geometric proportional limitation of Newton's Second Law; established the universal symbolic notation F = m * (dv/dt) = m * (d^2x/dt^2) that forms the foundation of all subsequent analytical dynamics.

Original Title & English Translation: De methodo fusiore et certiore solvendi problemata isoperimetrica (On a Broader and Surer Method of Solving Isoperimetric Problems)
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, May 1698, pp. 226–230
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated the two-ordinate variational technique: demonstrated that to vary a curve while preserving its total perimeter constraint (integral ds = L), one must vary two intermediate ordinates (delta y1, delta y2) simultaneously; established the necessity of Lagrange-type multiplier conditions.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the degrees-of-freedom bottleneck in constrained optimization; proved that single-point variations are fundamentally mathematically invalid for constrained functionals.

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematis de celerrimo descensu pro corporibus ad perpendiculum non cadentibus
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, June 1699, pp. 266–270
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Formulated brachistochrones under non-vertical force fields and motion constrained to inclined planes and cylinders; set up the differential variational equations for constrained 3D curved surfaces.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the planar Cartesian coordinate limitation of the brachistochrone; initiated variational dynamics on curved manifolds.

Original Title & English Translation: Du mouvement en général par toutes sortes de courbes, et des forces centrales, tant centrifuges que centripètes
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Paris: Histoire et Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences, Année 1700 (pub. 1703), pp. 83–101
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Decomposed acceleration along general 2D curved trajectories into tangential and normal differential components: a_t = dv/dt = v*dv/ds and a_n = v^2/rho; derived the general differential equation of central orbits in Cartesian coordinates.
Causal Bridge (Before -> After): Solved the restriction of differential mechanics to 1D rectilinear paths; provided the vector-component differential equations that Hermann (B3-028) and Euler (B3-059) developed into full orbital mechanics.

Original Title & English Translation: Solutio problematis isoperimetrici exhibita a Johanne Bernoulli
Publication Venue / Academy Archive: Leipzig: Acta Eruditorum, June 1700, pp. 261–266
The Puzzle Piece (Specific Contribution): Published an erroneous solution to Jakob's isoperimetric problem, attempting to bypass the two-ordinate variation by assuming a single varied point could satisfy the length constraint; triggered a legendary academic feud.
